text: Good morning everyone. I'd like to call to order the regular business meeting of City Council for this Wednesday, September 24th, as we gather on Treaty 6 territory and the traditional homeland of the May tea.
We are approaching the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, and I'm reminded that it was Indigenous peoples who first welcomed newcomers to this land.
Yet today too many Indigenous people do not feel welcome in their own home lands, and that is a tragedy we cannot ignore.
This truth is also a call to action. We are all treaty people with both the privilege and responsibility of being here.
Our responsibility is to do more than acknowledge the past. It is to walk together in the spirit of the treaties with honesty, respect and commitment to reconciliation.
That path is not easy, but it is one of hope because when we honor the treaties as they were intended as a promise of partnership, we can build a community and a city city where everyone belongs.

Knowing the two were good friends, it was only fitting that Lane provides some of the words about his colleague in here is what he had to say.
Shawn came to Saskatoon Transit just a few years ago. He had already been a driver for Winnipeg Transit and loved to share stories and differences between the two.
Shawn did not like to see or hear ill or unfair treatment or comments about anyone and was very quick to stop any he heard.
He would start his day on many occasions driving to work talking to his mom. Many of us saw it and it reinforced how much of a kind spirit he was.
His mom and his son and the things that they did were often talked about and shared. He was very proud of both of you.
Many of the people that have spoken about Shawn speak of his friendship, his humor and humility.
He is missed by his colleagues. Thank you Lane on behalf of the City of Saskatoon.
We want to send our condolences to the family and wish you peace.

And I would also like to let the family know that members of the Melgumated Transit Union are here and present today and we thank you for your leadership and for supporting the families that belong to the ATU.

Getting hundreds of new residences and homes onto the market over the next few years.
And so maintaining affordability, but increasing the availability of housing right across the housing spectrum is very important.

And for keeping things going.

Elder Korean led it and when it was over I was sitting beside her and she remarked, this is a great day.

Well on that note, I'm wanting to send a big shout out to the province of Saskatchewan for stepping out to support people who are in house in our community after years of trying to figure out stable finding especially in the winter time.

And the province has agreed to not only provide an additional $3 million an annual program to have places for people to be dropped in centers for youth for adults and special programming in the winters.
But also to have that gap filled for this year to ensure that we have you know the two warming centers that we're usually expecting including an opportunity for 24 seven.
So the people always have a safe place to get warm and and that the program at the youth both at the white.
The white buffalo youth center will also continue with an opportunity for an overnight option.

And I think that was part and parcel of the partnership between the province of Saskatchewan tribal council and the city of Saskatchewan where we have sort of been been demo demoing a bit of a hub model all summer long and how successful that was.
In terms of understanding how indigenous lead peacekeepers as part of that program to connect people to services has had a remarkable.
Change and promise of connecting more people to the services that they need.
So excited to see how that could be able to go forward on a on a more stable basis and continue forward.

Thank you your worship. So I've been getting a number of complaints and comments from the community recently this fall.
I understand we make adjustments to our transit system every year and this fall.
The 13 I believe was pulled out of loss nights and silverwood and people are left with service on the 17 and I'm getting a number complaints about a reduction in service.
I'm wondering if the administration can comment on why this change was made and what the rationale for it was.
Good morning your worship and council, Terry Schmidt, General Manager of Transportation and Construction. Thank you for the question.
Yeah, you are correct there was some changes made to service throughout the city that came into implementation June 29 of this year.

And the intent of those changes and the reason for those changes was to address capacity issues that were seen in some areas of the city with full buses and pass buys on some of the more high demand routes across the city.
And so to supplement the review, we also have been getting new buses.
No new buses started arriving last year.
They've continued to arrive this year.
We put several new buses into service already this fall and we're expecting more that will go into service.
So that is helping with some of the capacity issues that we are seeing.
But in addition to that the review was looking at schedules across the city where the planning team looked at different routes.
And if there was duplication or available capacity on some other routes throughout the city that we could reap balance.
Some of that available capacity or duplication to some of these other areas across the city where we're still seeing full buses.
And pass buys.
And so one of the areas identified with service duplication available capacity was the route 13 as it ran on the same route as route 30 through the lots of night's neighborhood.
So the previous route 13 operated only throughout the day during the use half fall and winter semesters.
And then the rest of the year just had limited morning and afternoon service.
So the rest of the route was covered by the 30.
So the route did not provide evening or weekend service.
And there were no reports of full buses or capacity issues on either route 13 or 30 in the past.
And so route 17 between stone bridge and useask did regularly report full buses and pass ups, particularly during useask.
And with high schools, transporting riders to high schools.
So as part of the rebalancing, routes 13 and 17 were combined to rebalance that capacity into one route.
The new combined route 17 and 13 does provide better overall service to all riders along this route corridor as it runs all days, weekends, evenings, and throughout the summer months now.
So the route 17 serves a lots of night neighborhood with 20 minute frequency during peak hours.
30 minute frequency and off peak and 45 minute frequency until the end of service, Sundays and staff holidays.
And most other routes in the city, they run 60 minute frequency during this time.
It also moves people and gives a new route from the north end of the city to the south end of the city without to need for transfer right from loss and down to stone bridge.
And so the changes have resulted as well in increased ridership on the combined routes of 17 and 13, then on the previous individual routes of 17 and 13.
So we're seeing an increase in ridership on that route.
And more reliable service with the 20 minute frequency out of loss and during peak times and the service on evenings and weekends.
So transit has been monitoring capacity.
We haven't got any reports of pass by's, our pass ups on route 17, leaving the Watson Heights Mall terminal since the changes.
And bus capacity is meeting the neighborhood demand.
Now we do recognize that this has resulted in a 15 minute transfer time if you're taking the 30 and you want to go to use ask on the 17 and we know that's not ideal.
So while we're going to continue to look at options that can reduce that transfer time, especially as new buses continue to arrive in the fall.
There also is another option to reduce that transfer time.
Riders could take the 30 and 35 right downtown to the terminal realizing it is a longer ride to the use ask.
But then the transfer time is seven and a half minutes.
So there is an option for a shorter transfer time.
It does require longer ride on the bus.
But as we get into the colder winter months, that may be something riders may want to look at you know looking at the offsets first of a longer ride versus a shorter transfer time.

As well we are still expecting more 40 foot buses.

We're going to continue to review across the city where we're seeing full buses, capacity issues, pass ups.
And then on a peri basis we'll look at putting more articulating buses on for additional capacity.

And if we can reduce that transfer time at loss and so we'll be looking at that overall in a peri basis across the city with the loss and transfer time as a part of that consideration.
